newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 100 -3 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 130 +6 on last week

AMLC COMMENTARY: There was again a fair amount of activity in beef and cattle markets this week. While the U.S. market came off the boil, prices in both the Japanese and South Korean markets increased and Australian cattle prices tracked higher

Australian exporters increased offer prices of product to Japan in light of the better returns available in the US market. Chilled grassfed fullset prices increased six U.S. cents/lb to 130 USc/lb this week, the first upward movement since the end of January.

Although the U.S. market eased this week, this was lost on domestic cattle markets which were shielded given the improvement in Asia, and the fact that cattle price rises, especially for manufacturing grades, still lag behind recent movements in export prices. Cow prices increased 12-14 c/kg dressed weight in markets across the major eastern states. Similar rises were evident for bullocks in Queensland. Across the other states, bullock price movements were positive, but small in comparison.

Trade cattle prices were subdued in New South Wales and Queensland but increased in South Australia and Victoria. In Victoria, restocker and feedlot buying drove prices higher for all young cattle grades. Prices rose 8.3c/kg liveweight across Victoria to average 97.3 c/kg clean.

Although spot supplies of lean beef in the US market remain tight, many end-users, having covered their immediate needs, paused for breath this week. This coupled with an increase in fed cuts entering grinding mixes, cooled prices for bull beef, cow beef and beef trimmings. Fresh U.S. domestic 90CL beef fell 9USc/lb to 101USc/lb but falls in imported prices were smaller,
frozen 90CL cow beef ending the week at 96USc/lb, down 4USc/lb.

Pressure on lean beef prices in the U.S. from fed cattle cuts is set to continue. Underlying the movement of fed beef cuts into grinding mixes has been the relatively subdued environment outside the U.S. lean beef complex.
More recently, increasing fed cattle slaughter rates have also had an impact.

The strengthening Australian dollar has worked against exporters this week, eroding returns despite firming export prices. Rain in Queensland saw cattle prices also firm, placing even greater pressure on exporters to receive better prices for

grassfed fullsets. Some exporters have commented that at current prices for chilled grassfed fullsets, it is better to break the fullset down and send it as frozen beef to stronger alternative markets such as the U.S. As a result, trade sources advise that shipments to Japan have not been as heavy as first anticipaated in early March.

The bankruptcy of two meat wholesalers in Japan this week has caused some concern to traders in the market. However, with the tariff decline imminent, the seasonal improvement in consumer demand and the approach of the Golden Week holiday, reports from Japan indicate that the market is starting to improve.
